newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures start narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures start narrowly mixed.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures started the day narrowly mixed as traders waited for Chicago National Association of Purchasing Management's (NAPM) monthly index.
They said the February index, which is expected to rise to 56.3, from 55.9 in January, could provide direction for both the U.S. stock and U.S. bond markets.
"If it's a bearish number it could get ugly in here," one Standard & Poor's 500 futures traders said.
Traders remain edgy about higher U.S. rates after comments made by the Federal Reserve chairman on Wednesday.
A sharp month-over-month rise in the overall Chicago NAPM index, or any of the sub-indices, would exacerbate those concerns, and possibly push bond prices lower and U.S. rates higher.
Traders said S&P futures would selloff in tandem with bonds.
One floor trader said a decline below 791.00, which is currently the daily low, in March S&Ps would "open the door to further losses." Some traders have put support at the 785.00 to 782.00 area.
At the open, one large firm and a large European bank each bought 500 March S&Ps, but initially failed to spark follow-through buying above 794.00.
Just before the number was released, March S&Ps rose to 794.40.
Fair value for March S&Ps is at 1.53 points to cash, with arbitrage buy programs at a premium of 2.70 points and arbitrage sell programs 0.95-point over.
Nikkei futures remained sharply lower on repatriation pressures overnight.
Traders noted active trading in Nikkei futures, as dealers rolled positions out of March and into June.
By mid-mornng, S&P futures had turned lower in line with losses in the U.S. bond market. March S&Ps fell to 790.00, through the support level of 791.00.

At 1012 CST/1612 GMT, March S&Ps were down 1.50 at 791.00, NYSE Composites were off 0.40 at 415.85, KCBT Value Lines were down 2.30 at 706.00, Nikkeis were down 460.0 at 18,510, Midcap 400s were down 0.70 at 261.20 and Nasdaq 100s were 6.75 lower at 840.00.
